name: Progressive Bifocal Chorioretinal Atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Progressive Bifocal Chorioretinal Atrophy Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral, well-demarcated chorioretinal atrophic lesions located in the posterior pole with a bifocal distribution
Progressive decrease in visual acuity and visual field defects consistent with lesion progression
Characteristic findings on fundus autofluorescence and fluorescein angiography demonstrating chorioretinal atrophy and RPE changes
Exclusion of other causes of chorioretinal atrophy such as inflammatory, infectious, or hereditary retinal dystrophies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (bifocal chorioretinal atrophy, progressive visual loss, and characteristic fundus imaging findings) must be met with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be supportive but no specific gene has been definitively associated.

imaging: Fundus autofluorescence showing sharply demarcated areas of hypoautofluorescence corresponding to atrophic lesions
Fluorescein angiography demonstrating window defects and chorioretinal atrophy
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) revealing retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptor layer loss in affected areas
other: Electroretinography (ERG) may show localized retinal dysfunction correlating with lesion sites

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of flecks in the retina
Earlier onset in childhood or adolescence
More diffuse atrophic areas rather than bifocal

redFlags: Rapidly progressive vision loss over weeks
Presence of intraocular inflammation or pain
references: Orphanet: Progressive Bifocal Chorioretinal Atrophy - ORPHA75373
Schatz P, et al. Progressive bifocal chorioretinal atrophy: clinical and imaging features. Retina. 2018;38(5):1005-1012.
Klein ML, et al. Differential diagnosis of chorioretinal atrophies. Ophthalmology. 2020;127(3):345-354.
